call_sites: reckon/cli.py:2454 the follower's attach line reads producer["stale"] off watch_stream_cursor (the prior finding's missing surface)
reckon/cli.py:3398 embeds project_watch_visibility in the crew status payload
reckon/mcp.py:3781 embeds it in the MCP status read
reckon/crew/runs.py:1355 watch_seat_version_current reads the same visibility

findings.text: the remedy the new line prints, "reckon crew watch --ensure-service --project X", is not a command: crew watch offers --ensure and no --ensure-service, so click refuses it with exit 2 and "No such option '--ensure-service'. Did you mean '--ensure'?", and the check added for the line pins the same invalid string at tests/test_producer_takes_new_code.py:476, so the one artifact a reader is told to run is the one thing the change makes certain does not work.

the line is written by _echo_follow_line from inside the _follow_watch_lines generator, which takes no JSON-mode argument and cannot know it, while every event the generator yields is routed by crew_follow through "if json_output: _emit(...)" (reckon/cli.py:2997, 3008, 3026, 3039); a consumer reading "crew follow --json" therefore receives one bare text line among JSON objects. Established by reading both code paths, not by a run.

the claim "red three runs of three without it and green three of three with it" is cited to logs/head-follower-freshness-isolated.log and logs/base-follower-freshness-isolated.log (the same pairing at docs/evidence/archive/the-fleet-counters-count-the-fleet-landed.html:461), each of which carries a single run and no arm, revision, warning or command header, so the artifacts show one red and one green run at an unstated revision and cannot support a count of three either way.

item_verdicts.diff: read commit by commit against e7c31ab7; 3efd388d carries both repairs and the three checks plus the two same-code controls, 0e5549ac carries only the pane-line declaration, and 0d242ae3 carries the plan comment, the evidence row and the figure.
item_verdicts.done_when: the done-when names three checks red at base and green at head, both same-code mutations, and the by-id family comparison, all under the run directory. logs/base-gate-2.log reads 3 failed / 0 passed at base e7c31ab7 with this node's file overlaid, logs/head-gate-3.log reads 6 passed at 3efd388d, and my own re-run in the reviewed worktree read 6 passed in 10.30s with module.__file__ resolving inside the producer worktree (logs/review-head-gate.log). The node's family logs are headed with arm, revision, tree and command (logs/base-watch-family-2.log:1-3, logs/head-watch-family-3.log:1-3) and the by-id block in the head log reads base 3 failed / 167 passed / 1 skipped and head 170 passed / 1 skipped with no head-only failure. The two same-code controls in negative-control-2.log redden exactly their own check. Two citations weaken the arm (FINDING docs/plans/the-fleet-counters-count-the-fleet.html:381).
item_verdicts.goal: the goal is that the two findings of the prior review are repaired at head 0d242ae3: a seat's recorded start time must belong to the process that wrote it, and the code stamp a seat records must reach a surface a reader uses. reckon/crew/runs.py:1692 gates the carry on the record's identity triple (pid, kernel pid start time, host) equalling this process's, which is exactly a replacement of the producer's own image, and a fresh arming over a dead predecessor's record restamps; the stamp reaches readers twice, as code_stamp and code_stale in project_watch_visibility (reckon/crew/runs.py:2333) embedded in the status payload at reckon/cli.py:3398 and reckon/mcp.py:3781, and as the follower's one attach line (reckon/cli.py:2454-2466). Both mechanisms are right; the line's remedy is not (FINDING reckon/cli.py:2465).
item_verdicts.write_paths: the declared paths for the repairs are reckon/crew/runs.py, reckon/cli.py, tests/test_producer_takes_new_code.py, tests/test_follower_freshness.py, the plan page, the cumulative evidence page and the figures directory; git diff --stat e7c31ab7..0d242ae3 lists exactly those seven (329 insertions, 10 deletions) and git status in the reviewed worktree is clean at 0d242ae3.

justifications.durability: the three checks are red at base and green at head, and the two same-code controls turn exactly their own check red and leave the other four passing, each naming its repair. Three points withheld: the check for the surfaced line asserts the invalid remedy string verbatim (tests/test_producer_takes_new_code.py:476), so it certifies the defect instead of catching it; and no check covers the line in --json mode (FINDING reckon/cli.py:2466).
justifications.evidence: the arms are headed and reproducible, the by-id comparison is explicit in the head family log (base 3 failed / 167 passed / 1 skipped, head 170 passed / 1 skipped, head-only none), the two same-code controls each redden their own check, and my independent re-run at head is green. Three points withheld: the 3-of-3 repetition claim is cited to two single-run logs that also carry no revision header (FINDING docs/plans/the-fleet-counters-count-the-fleet.html:381); and the same-code control that would catch the wrong remedy does not exist, because the check pins the wrong string instead (FINDING reckon/cli.py:2465). My own 31-file family run at head read 2 failed / 168 passed / 1 skipped, and I attribute both red rows to my own harness rather than to this change: I ran with --basetemp=/tmp/rev-prod-fam, and tests/test_watch_arming_isolation.py asserts a refusal whose detection keys on the throwaway root's name (reckon/crew/dispatch.py:148, ^(pytest-of-.+|pytest-\d+)$), so a renamed basetemp switches that guard off; re-running the file with a pytest-of-mcintos basetemp read 8 passed, and the node's own family runs used the default layout (logs/base-watch-family-2.log:12).
justifications.fit: the repairs sit in the modules that own them, watch_stream_cursor returns both stamps beside the verdict so a caller need not recompute one, and the identity triple reuse follows the form already used for arming guards, where pid alone is not sufficient to name a process. Two points withheld because the carried/restamped distinction appears only as an inline tuple comparison in _project_watch_claim without the sentence naming why the kernel start time is the part that carries the weight, and because the attach line writes itself into the follower's stream from inside the generator rather than through the event loop the stream's contract is defined by.
justifications.goal_fidelity: both prior findings are repaired at the right places: the carry is gated on the identity triple at runs.py:1692 so only a process that wrote the record itself can carry its start time, and the stamp is readable as code_stale in the status payload and printed on attach by the follower. Four points withheld because the repair's own operator-facing line names a command that cannot run: the remedy at cli.py:2465 is "reckon crew watch --ensure-service --project X" and crew watch's only flag is --ensure (cli.py:3110), so the line that exists to let a reader act sends them to click's "No such option" refusal (FINDING reckon/cli.py:2465).
justifications.scope_discipline: git diff --stat e7c31ab7..0d242ae3 lists exactly the seven declared paths with nothing outside them, git status --porcelain in the reviewed worktree is empty at head, and the change touches no shared index or sprint state.
